newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish crown firms with dollar, yields off lows.
newsitem.headline: Swedish crown firms with dollar, yields off lows.

text.p: Swedish debt yields picked up a touch after the fall of this morning, but stayed under Friday's closing levels, as the crown firmed along with the dollar.

"Debt yields closed at record lows on Friday. That's in itself a bullish signal. At the same time foreign markets were perfoming stronger this morning. But sellers soon entered the market," one dealer said.
"I don't think much will happen until the release of the U.S. NAPM figure," he added. The U.S. NAPM Index for November and U.S. October construction spending is due at 1500 GMT.
Six-month T-bill rates dropped one basis point to 4.17 percent and the ten year bond yield slid by the same amount to 6.97 percent.
The crown firmed to 4.3580 against the mark compared to 4.3600 late on Friday.
"I think the crown will firm further and break through 4.3550 against the mark," another dealer said.
From December 4 Danish bank Unibank will become a market maker of Swedish T-bills. The Debt Office now has 14 market makers in both state bonds and T-bills.
